name: Ars Technica

sources.title: Ars Technica Contact Us page — direct fetch blocked (403); submission form for tips/press releases exists here per secondary coverage
'Contacting Ken, a primer' — news tips go to news@arstechnica.com, forum moderation to mods@arstechnica.com (content read via search result)
Freelance interest inbox: freelance@arstechnica.com with subject 'freelancer interest' (content read via search result)

requirements: Not a directory — coverage is earned editorial; no listing product
News tips go to news@arstechnica.com; press releases to press@arstechnica.com; the contact page also hosts a tips submission form
Confidential material: PGP-encrypted email is supported (Mailvelope/Enigmail); some staff list PGP keys on the site
Freelance pitches go to freelance@arstechnica.com with subject 'freelancer interest'
Ars covers deep tech/science/IT policy — a SaaS launch needs a real technology or policy angle
preparation: A substantive tech/science/policy hook — Ars readers expect technical depth, not marketing copy
Concise tip email for news@arstechnica.com, or a press release for press@arstechnica.com
PGP setup (Mailvelope/Enigmail) if the material is sensitive
workflow: Decide the channel: news tip (news@arstechnica.com or the contact-page form), press release (press@arstechnica.com), or freelance pitch (freelance@arstechnica.com, subject 'freelancer interest')
Send a concise, technically literate tip — claim, evidence, why it matters
Coverage, if it happens, is a staff-written article — no listing page is created
watchFor: arstechnica.com blocks automated fetches (403) — the contact page itself could not be read directly this session
The inboxes documented on the site are old but still referenced; editors' direct emails exist but should not be mass-mailed
Freelance inbox historically receives too much mail to answer — silence is normal
A SaaS launch announcement alone is unlikely to earn coverage; Ars favors technically interesting stories
countsAsLive: An Ars Technica article mentioning or covering the product is published at arstechnica.com
unknowns: Whether the news@/press@ inboxes are still actively monitored under current Condé Nast operations
Whether the contact-page tips form still functions (page blocked to fetchers)
